items.question: Is a bare number with no unit (e.g. the legacy raw-millisecond `172800`) accepted as milliseconds?
items.ticket: Job timeouts are raw millisecond numbers in the config
items.chose: Rejects unit-less numbers as InvalidDuration, so existing raw-ms configs would fail to parse.
items.instead: Accept a bare integer as milliseconds for backward compatibility.

items.question: What is the largest duration that can be parsed or formatted?
items.chose: Caps totals at 2^53-1 ms; larger values are rejected on parse and on format.
items.instead: Allow anything up to u64::MAX, or use a smaller cap such as i64::MAX.

items.question: Can units be repeated or appear out of order (e.g. `30m1h`, `1h1h`)?
items.chose: Rejects them; each unit may appear at most once and must go in descending order h, m, s, ms.
items.instead: Accept any order and repeated units and sum them.

items.question: Which units are supported?
items.chose: Only h, m, s and ms; days (`d`) and others are rejected.
items.instead: Also accept d (and maybe w) for multi-day timeouts like the two-day example.

items.question: Are unit letters case-sensitive?
items.chose: Only lowercase units are accepted; `1H` and `1S` are rejected.

items.question: Is whitespace, a sign, or a decimal allowed (e.g. `1h 30m`, ` 1h`, `+1s`, `1.5h`)?
items.chose: Rejects all of them, along with empty input.
items.instead: Trim surrounding whitespace, allow spaces between parts, or allow fractional values.

items.question: Are zero values and leading zeros accepted when parsing?
items.chose: Accepts `0s`, `0ms` and `01h`, and returns 0 for zero values.
items.instead: Reject zero durations (a zero timeout is meaningless), or reject leading zeros.

items.question: How is an overflowing or oversized number handled when parsing?
items.chose: Maps integer-parse failure, multiplication or addition overflow, and a total above the cap all to the same InvalidDuration error.
items.instead: Use a separate overflow or out-of-range error variant.

items.question: What does formatting 0 ms print?
items.ticket: print them back in the same style in the admin UI

items.question: How does formatting choose among equivalent representations?
items.ticket: print them back in the same style in the admin UI
items.chose: Picks the fewest-character string, so 90 s prints as "90s", 5,400,000 ms as "90m" and 1,500 ms as "1500ms", with ties going to fewer parts.
items.instead: Use a greedy largest-unit decomposition, giving "1h30m", "1m30s" and "1s500ms".

items.question: What happens when formatting a value above the supported maximum?
What error text is shown on a parse or format failure?
items.chose: A single generic message per error that lists the expected syntax and the maximum, with no detail about which part of the input was bad.
items.instead: Include the offending input or position in the message.
